meta.dataset: Punctual Pros market context: Central Pennsylvania and Jersey Shore (competitors, Authority Brands franchise territories, incentives, county profiles, market signals)
meta.method: Competitors came from ZoomInfo company searches (radius around Lancaster 17601, Toms River 08753, Chambersburg 17201 and Reading 19601), Google News RSS deal searches, and fetches of each company website for founding year, reviews and ownership claims. PE and utility ownership is stated only where a deal article or company page confirms it. Franchise territories were parsed from the official One Hour, Benjamin Franklin Plumbing and Mister Sparky location directories (PA, NJ, MD, DE); each location page was fetched for rating, license and team names, and PP/Horvath affiliation is graded confirmed, likely, possible or no_public_evidence. Incentives come from utility, IRS and agency pages plus news of program status. County profiles use ACS 2020-2024 5-year tables (via the Census Reporter API, because api.census.gov now requires a key), Census PEP vintage 2025 county estimates, and Census Building Permits Survey 2024/2025 annual county files. Market signals are fetched news, trade-press and BLS OEWS May 2025 wage data.
sources_summary: Census Building Permits Survey county annual files (co2024a, co2025a)
caveats: ACS data is the 2020-2024 5-year release (one vintage newer than the ACS 2023 requested), pulled from the Census Reporter mirror because api.census.gov returned 'Missing Key'. Values match Census tables but are not the 2023 vintage.

PP ownership is confirmed only for the Lancaster (Running Pump Rd) tri-brand site and the Beachwood NJ Horvath sites. Harrisburg, York and West Chester are 'likely' (co-located tri-brand sites in counties LNP says PP serves; Franchise Times says 4 brick-and-mortar + 1 satellite). Levittown and Lansdale are 'possible'. Location pages do not name franchisees.
A Pleasantville NJ tri-brand operator trades as 'The Punctual Pros' (thepunctualprosnj.com). Its relationship to Broad Sky's Punctual Pros is unverified.

The brief lists Haller Enterprises as PE-backed, but no deal announcement was found (a PitchBook snippet calls it a private company; one Glassdoor review says PE-owned). Ownership is left null and marked unverified.

Employee counts are mostly ZoomInfo estimates and can understate multi-site firms (e.g., UGI HVAC shows 47). Review counts and ratings are shown only where a company page displayed them. Brand-wide aggregates (4.82 / 200,251 and 4.82 / 125,662) on franchise pages were set to null.

Competitor coverage is broad in the Lancaster, Harrisburg, York, Berks and Ocean/Monmouth cores but thin in Montgomery and Chester, where many Philadelphia-suburb operators exist. Several NJ sites (Point Bay Fuel, Care Temp, A. Bailey, Premier Climate Care, Aggressive Mechanical) blocked retrieval and were excluded.

PECO and JCP&L rebate dollar amounts could not be retrieved (JS-rendered or connection refused). FirstEnergy PA (Met-Ed) says it is 'working to finalize new programs' for Act 129 Phase V, so amounts are null.
NJ HEAR/HOMES status after Sept 2025 is unverified. PA Penn Energy Savers was still 'proposed' as of July 2026.
An apparent 'Lennar Roselyn Lancaster 1,860-unit' development in search results is in Lancaster, South Carolina, and was excluded.

Web search quota was exhausted. Discovery used Google News RSS and ZoomInfo, and every item's primary source_url was fetched directly. Some secondary URLs (Business Wire, NJ.com, PennLive, Capital-Star, Glassdoor) returned 403 or paywalls and are cited from search results only.

NJBIZ cites NJ DCA data showing 859 housing units authorized in Monmouth in 2025. The Census BPS county file shows 2,138 total units (1,481 single-family) for 2025. Sources and definitions differ; county_profile uses Census BPS.
Smith + Howard (BSP's exited portfolio company) is out of scope and excluded.
meta.territory_summary: 1) Punctual Pros' nine-county Central PA core (Lancaster, York, Dauphin, Cumberland, Berks, Lebanon, Franklin, Adams, Perry) holds about 2.51M people and 965k occupied homes. PP also serves the Chester, Montgomery and Bucks fringe and, through Horvath, Ocean and Monmouth counties in NJ (about 1.32M people, 496k households). 2) The housing stock is old and owner-occupied: 45-64% of units were built before 1980, median build years run 1969-1983, and owner-occupancy runs 63-82%. That is a large, recurring replacement and repair base. 3) Heating fuel splits the territory. About 241k core-PA households (and about 390k across all 13 counties) still heat with fuel oil or propane: 44.5% in Perry, 37.6% Lebanon, 30.0% Berks, 27.7% Adams, 25.2% Lancaster. Ocean and Monmouth are 78-81% utility gas. 4) Growth is concentrated in the Cumberland-York-Adams corridor (+6.9%, +3.7%, +3.6% population 2020-25) and in Ocean County (+5.7%, the most single-family permits in the footprint at 2,808 in 2024 and 2,372 in 2025). Dauphin and Monmouth are slow-growth or declining in permits. 5) PP's confirmed tri-brand sites are Lancaster (Running Pump Rd) and Beachwood NJ (Horvath). Tri-brand sites in Harrisburg, York and West Chester are likely PP. There is no One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky location in Berks, Lebanon, Franklin, Adams or Perry. 6) Competition is densest in Lancaster, Dauphin and Chester: Haller (about 400 employees, 9.4k reviews), HB McClure (about 1,000 employees, ESOP), UGI HVAC (utility), Brubaker (ESOP). PE-backed rivals are Sila (Goldman Sachs Alternatives), Len The Plumber (Neffsville, L Catterton), P1/Essig (Berks) and Horizon (New Mountain) in the SE fringe. 7) Demand drivers for 2026 are mixed. Federal 25C/25D credits ended Dec 31, 2025, and PA's $258M Penn Energy Savers rebates remain unlaunched. Utility rebates are modest in PA (PPL heat pumps $225-325; UGI gas furnace $500, boilers $1,200-1,500; FirstEnergy PA programs in transition) but rich in NJ (NJNG SAVEGREEN up to $3,650 HVAC and $4,000 hybrid heat plus $25k 0% financing through June 30, 2027). 8) Tailwinds include record Lancaster home prices ($385k median, June 2026), rising electric rates (PPL, JCP&L), July 2026 heat-wave and flood events, and a deep technician pipeline at Thaddeus Stevens (enrollment 875 to 1,491). Local HVAC median wages are about $60-63k in PA MSAs and $78k in the NY-NJ MSA, against PP's posted $70-120k tech range.

expansion_thesis.move: Densify the Cumberland-York-Adams growth corridor from the Harrisburg and York sites
expansion_thesis.evidence: Cumberland +6.9% population 2020-25 (fastest PA county in set), median sale price $369,995 (+9.5% y/y). York has the most PA single-family permits (952 in 2024, 1,025 in 2025). Adams +3.6%. York has no PE-backed competitor tracked.
expansion_thesis.targets: Tuck-ins among West Shore and York independents: Pronto/SECCO (about 52 employees), Central Penn Plumbing (about 51 employees, 1,363 reviews), Zimmerman, Advance HAWS, RiverView Mechanical, R.D. Heller.

expansion_thesis.move: Enter Berks (Reading) and Lebanon, whitespace for the tri-brand
expansion_thesis.evidence: No One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky location in Berks or Lebanon. Berks has 163k households, 63.6% built before 1980 (oldest in set), and 48.9k oil and propane homes (30.0%). Lebanon has 37.6% oil and propane and only 0.3% of homes for sale, so owners repair in place. The 537-unit Cumru Twp development and Highland Place 55+ add new-build demand. Competition is UGI HVAC plus a fragmented field; P1 already took Essig, so move before Sila (Palmyra) extends east.
expansion_thesis.targets: Platform tuck-in in Reading (e.g., Trinity Comfort about 72 employees, Gehringer Mechanical tri-trade, M&M Mechanical), paired with securing Authority Brands territory rights for Berks and Lebanon zip codes.

expansion_thesis.move: Launch an oil and propane to heat-pump / hybrid conversion engine
expansion_thesis.evidence: About 241k oil and propane households in the core (Lancaster 53.6k, Berks 48.9k, York 36.5k, Dauphin 24.7k, Cumberland 22.2k, Lebanon 21.3k). With 25C gone, the offer needs financing plus PPL rebates ($225-325), and UGI's $500-1,500 gas incentives where gas mains exist. Enrolling techs in DEP's Penn Heat Pump Pathways pre-qualifies PP for Penn Energy Savers (up to $8,000 per heat pump, up to $14,000 per LMI household) if DOE releases the $258M.
expansion_thesis.targets: Service departments or customer books of fuel dealers: SOC Energy (Harrisburg/Lancaster, 1922), W.C. Eshenaur (1928), Countryside Fuel (Lebanon), Aero Energy (Adams; ESOP, so partnership is likelier than a sale).

expansion_thesis.move: Scale Horvath from Ocean into Monmouth
expansion_thesis.evidence: Ocean is the fastest-growing county in the footprint (+5.7%, about 36k residents 2020-25, JCP&L $108M grid build and 50+ MW of new connection requests, 2,372 single-family permits in 2025). Monmouth has the highest income ($124,845), 81% gas heat, and NJNG SAVEGREEN pays up to $3,650 HVAC and $4,000 hybrid heat with $25k 0% OBRP. Neither county has a PE platform tracked.
expansion_thesis.targets: The separate Manalapan One Hour and Mister Sparky franchisee(s) (a repeat of the Horvath franchise-to-franchise playbook). Independents: Dash Mechanical (about 92 employees, Brick), Lawes (Shrewsbury, 1926), Air Experts, Garden State AC, Eastern Shore HVAC.

expansion_thesis.move: Authority Brands franchisee roll-up in adjacent mid-Atlantic markets
expansion_thesis.evidence: Tri-brand co-located operators near PP with strong review bases: Wilmington DE (One Hour 4.9 / 3,276; Ben Franklin 4.9 / 3,400; 410 Meco Dr), Dover DE, Bel Air/Harford MD, Mount Airy MD (One Hour 4.7 / 863), Bethlehem PA (Ben Franklin). A Pleasantville NJ operator trades as 'The Punctual Pros'; confirm whether it is related before treating it as a target.
expansion_thesis.targets: Operators within about 90 minutes of Lancaster that already share PP's brand system, which means lower integration risk. Apex's $10B valuation (May 2026) and Sila's Goldman backing show platform exit multiples reward mid-Atlantic density.

expansion_thesis.move: Deprioritize organic push in Dauphin new construction and Franklin/Perry greenfield
expansion_thesis.evidence: Dauphin single-family permits fell to 180 in 2025 from 287 in 2024, and HB McClure and Haller dominate. Franklin and Perry are low-density; enter via small tuck-ins or satellite trucks, not new branches.

items.name: PPL Electric Utilities - residential heating & cooling rebates (Air-Source Heat Pump)
items.eligibility: PPL Electric residential customers; ENERGY STAR certified equipment; apply via PPL rebate portal
items.dates: Program year beginning June 1, 2026 (Act 129 Phase V)
items.notes: PPL's rebate overview says 'Receive up to $500 each on heating and cooling upgrades'; mini-split $225; insulation up to $575 each.

items.name: PPL Electric Utilities - ENERGY STAR mini-split heat pump rebate
items.measure: ENERGY STAR certified mini-split heat pump
items.notes: Ductless mini-splits suit oil and propane homes without ductwork.

items.name: PPL Electric - income-based offers & WRAP
items.measure: Enhanced rebates, no-cost assessments and improvements for income-qualified customers
items.notes: Enhanced income-based rebates; amounts not published on overview page.

items.name: FirstEnergy Pennsylvania (Met-Ed/Penelec/Penn Power/West Penn) - residential HVAC rebates
items.sponsor: FirstEnergy Pennsylvania (Met-Ed serves much of York, Adams, Berks, Lebanon; Penn Power/West Penn serve Franklin)
items.measure: HVAC rebates, appliance rebates, audits (Act 129 Phase V)
items.status: in transition - 'working to finalize new programs' (Sept 2026)
items.notes: Appliance recycling remains active ($50 refrigerator or room AC; $25 freezer, dehumidifier or mini fridge). HVAC rebate amounts are not posted. The EnergySavePA program portal did not connect.

items.name: UGI Utilities - natural gas home rebates
items.measure: ENERGY STAR gas furnace $500; 94+ AFUE boiler $1,200; 94+ AFUE combi boiler $1,500; ENERGY STAR tankless water heater $400; boiler reset controls $300; 94+ AFUE SPVU $450; direct-vent fireplace insert $150; smart thermostat $50
items.eligibility: UGI gas customers in PA (Maryland UGI gas customers not eligible)
items.notes: Supports high-efficiency gas replacement jobs in UGI territory.

items.name: UGI Utilities - electric-to-gas heating conversion & electric rebates
items.measure: Switch electric primary heating to natural gas (up to $1,500); smart thermostat $50; appliance recycling $75 fridge/freezer, $50 room AC/dehumidifier
items.notes: UGI Electric's service area is mostly outside PP's core. Included for completeness.

items.name: NJ Natural Gas SAVEGREEN - HVAC & water heating rebates + 0% OBRP
items.measure: High-efficiency gas furnace (95% AFUE), ASHP/ccASHP, tankless water heater (UEF>=0.95); must replace non-condensing furnace/boiler
items.amount_usd: up to 3650 rebate; up to 25000 at 0% APR on-bill repayment
items.eligibility: NJNG residential customers; existing homes only (not new construction); photo of old equipment and permit required; apply within 120 days; income-qualified +$300 per equipment
items.dates: Equipment purchased and installed by June 30, 2027
items.notes: The main demand lever for Horvath's Ocean and Monmouth market.

items.name: NJ Natural Gas SAVEGREEN - Hybrid Heat (dual-fuel heat pump) rebate
items.measure: Hybrid heat: gas furnace/boiler + ducted or ductless ASHP + integrated thermostat
items.amount_usd: up to 2000 single-zone / up to 4000 two-zone
items.eligibility: NJNG customers; ccASHP SEER2>=15.2, EER2>=10, HSPF2>=8.1, COP>=1.75 at 5F for two-zone max
items.notes: Plus up to $25,000 0% OBRP financing.

items.name: JCP&L (FirstEnergy NJ) - residential HVAC & appliance rebates
items.measure: ENERGY STAR central AC, air-source heat pumps, ductless mini-split heat pumps, furnace fans, smart thermostats (contractor-installed); heat pump water heaters (appliance rebates)
items.status: active (amounts not published on FirstEnergy page)
items.notes: The program site energysavenj.com refused connections on 2026-09-24, so amounts are unverified.

items.name: New Jersey Clean Energy Program (NJBPU) - statewide programs
items.measure: Statewide clean energy incentives; residential efficiency delivered largely through utility programs (NJNG SAVEGREEN, JCP&L)
items.notes: The homepage currently features a proposed Garden State Energy Storage program. No standalone heat-pump dollar amounts are posted.

items.name: Federal Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit (IRC 25C)
items.measure: 30% of qualified costs; up to $2,000/yr for heat pumps & HPWH, $1,200/yr other improvements
items.eligibility: Property placed in service Jan 1, 2023 - Dec 31, 2025
items.status: expired for 2026 - no credit for property placed in service after Dec 31, 2025 (terminated early by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, July 2025)
items.notes: WHYY: about 239,000 PA, DE and NJ households claimed $205M for tax year 2023. Losing the credit likely pulled heat-pump demand into 2H 2025 and leaves a 2026 air pocket.

items.name: Federal Residential Clean Energy Credit (IRC 25D)
items.measure: 30% of solar, geothermal heat pumps, battery storage, etc.
items.status: expired - not available for property placed in service after Dec 31, 2025
items.notes: Geothermal heat-pump jobs lose the 30% credit in 2026.

items.name: Penn Energy Savers (PA DEP HEAR + HOMES, IRA-funded)
items.measure: HEAR rebates for LMI households: heat pump for space heating/cooling $8,000; HPWH $1,750; electric load service center $4,000; wiring $2,500; insulation/air sealing/ventilation $1,600; up to $14,000 per household
items.eligibility: Low- and moderate-income households; qualified contractors only
items.status: not launched - on hold since March 2025 pending U.S. DOE approval (Aug 2025); still described as a 'proposed program' in July 2026
items.notes: $258M program. PP should register as a qualified contractor now, which the Penn Heat Pump Pathways training route enables. Large upside if DOE releases the funds.

items.name: New Jersey Home Energy Rebates (HEAR/HOMES, IRA-funded)
items.status: not launched as of Sept 2025 (BPU targeted end-2025 launch pending DOE final approval); 2026 status unverified

items.name: PA Whole-Home Repairs Program
items.measure: Grants for habitability/energy repairs incl. HVAC, plumbing, electrical for LMI homeowners
items.status: state funding lapsed - left out of 2025-26 PA budget (Dec 2025); program adopted as a national pilot in the federal 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (June 2026)
items.notes: $125M initial 2022-23 appropriation; about 4,000 homes repaired statewide. County grant flow for HVAC replacements is effectively paused until new money arrives.

items.name: PA LIHEAP 2025-26 (Cash + Crisis)
items.measure: Heating-bill cash grants and crisis grants for heating emergencies (incl. broken heating equipment)
items.status: 2025-26 season extended to May 8, 2026; $100 supplemental benefit from leftover funds (Jul 2026)
items.notes: By March 21, 2026 it had reached 233,000+ households with cash grants and about 83,000 with crisis grants. Crisis grants fund emergency furnace repairs.

items.name: Lancaster County median home sale price hits record $385,000 (June 2026)
items.detail: Median sold price $385,000, $20,000 above prior record; 570 closed sales (+33.8% m/m); 544 new listings; 20 days on market; 104.2% of list.
items.implication: Rising turnover and prices support pre-sale inspections, replacements and upgrades in PP's HQ county.

items.name: Greater Harrisburg home sales +8.7% y/y, median +9.3% (June 2026)
items.detail: GHAR area: 678 closed sales, median $329,950 (+9.3%), active listings +17.4%. Cumberland closed sales +15.9%, median $369,995 (+9.5%).
items.implication: Cumberland is the fastest-growing PA county in the footprint and sells the priciest homes. Prioritize West Shore marketing from the Harrisburg site.

items.name: JCP&L invests $108M in Ocean County grid to meet 'explosive growth'
items.geography: Ocean County, NJ (Lakewood, Jackson, Toms River)
items.detail: Ocean County added nearly 30,000 residents 2020-2024; developers applied for 50+ MW of new connections in a year (~50,000 homes' worth). Line upgrades in Lakewood (incl. Leisure Village), Jackson, Toms River.
items.implication: Horvath's Beachwood base sits in the fastest-growing county in the footprint, so new-home and service demand should keep compounding.

items.name: Monmouth County housing boom: 859 units permitted in 2025; Monmouth Mall redevelopment adds 1,000 apartments
items.detail: NJ DCA data: Monmouth had the 3rd-most housing units authorized in NJ in 2025 (859), 29% multifamily. Kushner's Monmouth Mall redevelopment includes 1,000 multifamily units. 76% owner-occupied; median value $606,100.
items.implication: High-income, high-value homes make Monmouth the best NJ ticket-size market. Multifamily adds service-contract opportunities.

items.name: Cumru Township (Berks) reviews 537-unit mixed development
items.detail: Plans off Route 10 north of Flying Hills: 256 apartments, 175 townhouses, 106 single-family homes, plus commercial and 30 acres of open space.
items.implication: New-construction pipeline in Berks, where no Authority Brands (One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky) location exists today.

items.name: THP Homes plans Highland Place 55+ community in Berks
items.detail: Reading Eagle reports THP Homes bringing the Highland Place 55+ development to Berks County (unit count not captured).
items.implication: Age-restricted buyers favor service agreements and maintenance memberships.

items.name: Ocean County seniors fear being priced out of retirement housing
items.detail: Jersey Shore Online reports affordability pressure in Ocean County's large age-restricted housing stock. NJ.com (Apr 2026) reported affordable rentals at a Barnegat 55+ community from $1,438/month.
items.implication: Ocean's large 55+ base (Leisure Village and similar) wants fixed-price service plans and financing, not premium replacements.

items.name: July 2026 heat wave: firefighters hose down Met-Ed substations in Adams County; PJM near-record demand
items.detail: On July 3, 2026, several fire companies cooled transformers at Met-Ed substations in Straban and Mt. Joy townships. WHYY (July 2) reported the Philly-area heat wave could push PJM demand to record levels.
items.implication: Peak AC failure season. Capacity to handle same-day no-cool calls is a share-gain lever in 2026-27 summers.

items.name: Severe July 2026 storms flood Monmouth/Ocean communities
items.detail: CBS New York: severe flooding after strong storms; roof collapse at a BJ's in Ocean Township; gas and refrigerant leaks reported (Monmouth County Sheriff).
items.implication: Drives sump-pump, water-heater, backflow and electrical-panel work for Ben Franklin and Mister Sparky Ocean County.

items.name: JCP&L seeks 8.8% electric rate increase (effective Jan 2028) after July 4 storm outages
items.detail: Average residential bill +$14.23/month (~$170/yr) for 767 kWh; $253M base distribution increase; would not hit bills until January 2028.
items.implication: Rising electric bills support high-efficiency heat-pump and hybrid-heat sales in NJ and the NJNG SAVEGREEN hybrid-heat pitch.

items.name: PPL price-to-compare rises to 13.147 cents/kWh June 1, 2026; distribution +3.23% July 1
items.detail: Price to compare rises from 12.953 to 13.147 cents/kWh (~1.5%) on June 1, 2026, then distribution rates rise 3.23% on July 1.
items.implication: Higher electric costs strengthen the efficiency-upgrade case, especially replacing old electric-resistance and heat-pump systems.

items.name: Natural-gas price surge threatens PA winter heating bills (2025-26)
items.detail: EIA had forecast Northeast gas heating costs -1% and electric +3% for winter 2025-26, but gas prices then surged. The article also notes LIHEAP was on pause at the time.
items.implication: High fuel costs push homeowners to tune-ups and efficiency replacements.

items.name: High HVAC equipment prices are structural; repair share of revenue up to 31.3%
items.detail: ACHR News: minimum-SEER units are about 70% of Lennox sales. Housecall Pro data show repair revenue share rose from 21.6% (2021) to 31.3% (2025) as homeowners repair rather than replace.
items.implication: Mix shift toward repair and maintenance favors membership-plan density over replacement volume. Plan the replacement-to-repair mix accordingly.

items.name: EPA final rule removes Jan 1, 2026 R-410A residential install deadline
items.detail: The EPA Technology Transitions rule revision lets existing R-410A inventory be installed indefinitely. Industry groups warn refrigerant prices may rise.
items.implication: Eases A2L transition cost pressure on 2026 installs, but refrigerant cost inflation hits service margins.

items.name: Thaddeus Stevens College builds new residence and dining hall; enrollment nearly doubled since 2013
items.detail: Enrollment grew from 875 to 1,491 since 2013. New 150-bed residence hall plus 500-seat dining hall (estimated $40M), completion in 18-24 months.
items.implication: PP's HQ is minutes from the largest trade-college pipeline in the region. A formal hiring partnership is a low-cost technician-supply moat.

items.name: Penn College and Thaddeus Stevens sign HVACR articulation agreement
items.detail: Graduates of Thaddeus Stevens' HVACR associate degree can continue into Penn College programs.
items.implication: More credentialed HVACR grads in the pipeline, and more competition for them from HB McClure, Haller and others.

items.name: Thaddeus Stevens expands trades training (incl. HVAC and plumbing) to North Philadelphia
items.detail: Programs at Esperanza Tec Centro Philadelphia include Commercial-Industrial HVAC and Commercial-Industrial Plumbing, with Thaddeus Stevens as partner.
items.implication: Wider Stevens footprint in SE PA. Possible recruiting channel for PP's Chester and Montgomery sites.

items.name: PA DEP launches Penn Heat Pump Pathways ($4.9M DOE grant) to train HVAC workers
items.detail: Statewide program run by the Home Performance Coalition to recruit, train and upskill HVAC workers on heat pumps. Completers may qualify as Penn Energy Savers contractors (up to $14,000 per-household rebates if launched).
items.implication: Enrolling PP techs positions the company to capture Penn Energy Savers rebates if DOE releases the funds.

items.name: Punctual Pros posts HVAC Service Technician (Lancaster) at $70,000-$120,000/yr
items.detail: HVACJobsHQ lists one open Punctual Pros role: HVAC Service Technician, Lancaster, PA, $70,000-$120,000 per year, full time.
items.implication: PP's posted range sits well above the BLS median for HVAC mechanics in the Lancaster MSA ($60,530), which implies a premium for experienced service techs.

items.name: Lebanon County housing shortage: only 0.3% of homes for sale
items.detail: Commissioners were told only 0.3% of the county's for-sale homes are available (a healthy market is 2-3%) and renters have very few choices.
items.implication: Tight supply means aging owner-occupied stock, 61% built before 1980, gets repaired and upgraded rather than sold.

items.name: Apex Service Partners valued at $10B in Apollo minority deal
items.detail: Apollo to invest about $2B alongside Alpine Investors; Apex has 75 local brands in 46 states, 13,000+ employees and over $3B revenue.
items.implication: Platform valuations keep rising and national roll-ups remain active buyers. Supports exit multiples for a scaled mid-Atlantic PP.

items.name: Service Experts pivots to franchising (announced late 2025)
items.detail: Service Experts (about 80 locations in 31 states, about $1B revenue) now offers franchises via greenfield and conversion paths and is deprioritizing M&A.
items.implication: A new franchise brand may recruit Central PA and NJ independents as conversions, competing with PP for the same tuck-in targets.

items.name: Sila Services: Goldman Sachs Alternatives investment and continued PA tuck-ins
items.detail: Sila (40+ brands) closed the Goldman Sachs Alternatives investment (announced Nov 2024), then added Sullivan Super Service (Pittsburgh, Jan 2025) and Oxford Plumbing & Heating (Chester County, Oct 2025) after Triangle (Nov 2023) and ECS Comfort (Feb 2024).
items.implication: Sila is the most active PE buyer in PP's footprint and will compete for Lebanon, Dauphin and Chester tuck-ins.
